name: remit-exec-with-role
description: Read the Safe's state, preflight the call against the Roles Modifier, execute it through execTransactionWithRole, notify the operator channel.

nodes.purpose: Read the Safe's balance, the Roles instance and the agent's membership, so the run is decided on current state rather than on what the strategy believed.
eth_call execTransactionWithRole with shouldRevert=true. Returns a named Status on refusal. This is G2: no gas is spent whatever the answer.
Submit execTransactionWithRole. The only path by which value leaves the Safe. Retries and private routing are enabled on the workflow, not in our code.
Post the outcome and the transaction hash to the operator channel.
nodes.note: KH-6. The operator hears about an execution from KeeperHub, not from us: a notification that depends on our process being alive is a notification that goes missing exactly when it matters.

notes: This document is Remit's declaration of what must run. It is authored here and hashed into the Remit as workflowHash.

It is NOT KeeperHub's serialisation of a registered workflow: that shape is whatever the console stores when this is registered, and nobody has registered it — so the bridge takes the direct-execution route and the receipt records which route ran.

P3 registers this workflow, records the id KeeperHub assigns, and reconciles the two. If KeeperHub's canonical definition differs, the Remit is reissued against the registered hash — a Remit is cheap, a wrong binding is not.
KH-5. Private routing and retry are the workflow's, not ours. Remit has no
resubmission path of its own: two systems deciding when to resend the same
intent is how an execution layer double-spends.
Evidence for a run lives in KeeperHub's own run log — `kh run logs <run-id>`,
or GET /api/execute/{executionId}/status — and the receipt records the
executionId that log is addressed by.
